# Security Requirements Checklist: Secure image-URL fetching (credential containment + relay hardening)

**Purpose**: Requirements-quality review of the credential-containment and relay-hardening specification before/during implementation review
**Created**: 2026-11-10
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `$speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Are all channels by which a credential could reach a non-provider host enumerated and covered (keychain fetch, streaming transport, model discovery, Copilot session traffic)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001, Spec §FR-004]
- [ ] CHK002 Is the credential allowlist definition complete (which host, which comparison axes: case, trailing dot, port, subdomains)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002]
- [ ] CHK003 Are all non-public address classes the relay must refuse enumerated exhaustively (loopback, link-local, private, unique-local, unspecified, CGNAT — and the additional multicast/reserved classes)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-005]
- [ ] CHK004 Are both transfer bounds specified with values and with the behavior on exceedance (relay cut-off, client null-materialization)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-007]
- [ ] CHK005 Is the failure-mode matrix for a blocked/dead/oversized image complete (user-visible outcome, persistence of the reply, turn outcome)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-008]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK006 Is "credential header" defined precisely enough that an implementer knows exactly which headers the relay strips? [Clarity, Spec §FR-004, contracts/llm-proxy.md]
- [ ] CHK007 Is the strip-vs-reject distinction unambiguous (credentials stripped silently; targets rejected with a distinct status)? [Clarity, Spec §FR-004 vs §FR-005]
- [ ] CHK008 Is the host-comparison rule testable as stated (exact equality after normalization, ports ignored, no wildcards)? [Measurability, Spec §FR-002]
- [ ] CHK009 Is the redirect policy stated as an absolute (never follow) rather than left to per-call discretion? [Clarity, Spec §FR-006]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK010 Does the browser-direct loopback exemption (local runtimes) coexist consistently with the client-side credential rule and the relay's public-target rule? [Consistency, Spec §Edge Cases, §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK011 Are the two layers (client gate, relay enforcement) specified as independent controls such that either alone prevents the leak? [Consistency, Spec §US1, §US2]
- [ ] CHK012 Do FR-009's "unchanged legitimate flows" and FR-004's "strip on undeclared host" conflict for any named producer (Copilot, discovery, local runtimes)? [Consistency, Spec §FR-004, §FR-009]

## Scenario & Edge Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK013 Are keyless-provider + foreign-host image URLs covered (no missing-key failure introduced)? [Coverage, Spec §US1 Scenario 3]
- [ ] CHK014 Are obfuscated address forms (hex/octal IPv4, IPv4-mapped IPv6, brackets) addressed as edge cases? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK015 Is the redirect-from-provider-host-to-attacker-host scenario addressed? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK016 Is the unresolvable-hostname outcome specified for both layers (relay fail-closed; client notice)? [Coverage, Spec §US2 Scenario 6, §FR-008]
- [ ] CHK017 Is the DNS-rebinding TOCTOU residual risk explicitly scoped and accepted? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK018 Are the two issue-mandated regression cases traceable from spec to measurable success criteria (SC-001/SC-002) and to fail-first test tasks? [Traceability, Spec §FR-010, tasks.md T005/T011–T012]
- [ ] CHK019 Can "no legitimate-flow regression" (SC-003) be objectively verified by the named suites? [Measurability, Spec §SC-003]
- [ ] CHK020 Is the no-CDN-allowlist default documented as a decision with its reversal path (add later without protocol change)? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `$speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `$speckit-specify` and `$speckit-clarify`
- Generated autonomously (fleet leader run): depth Standard, audience PR reviewer, focus clusters = credential containment + relay target safety; clarifying-question step skipped per orchestration instructions (defaults applied per checklist command rules).
